transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. It's been on my mind a lot. And lately, I've just been saying that I really don't need to see another winter. So, they wanted me to come in and talk to you.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?

Well, no, I'm not going to do anything right this minute. It's more just... like I was saying, it's this constant thought that they'd be better off if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. I don't have a specific plan to do something today, but I really meant it when I said I don't want to see another winter. I just feel like I'm done, and it would be easier for everyone if I just passed on.
Have you been feeling depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

I'm not really sure if I'd call it depressed. I don't think I feel sad or down, if that's what you mean. I haven't really noticed feeling like that. It's more just... well, like I said, I just feel tired of it all. I feel like I'm finished. But I don't know if I'd say I'm walking around feeling depressed every day.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I suppose I have. I used to... well, I used to look forward to a lot of things. Playing bridge, working out in the garden, helping with the cooking at church... even going to Cubs games. But now, I just sit in my chair. I can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore.
Did all of this start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yes, I suppose it did. This has all been going on since my bowling partner died. That was about a year and a month ago.
Have you been feeling this way most days for the past year since your bowling partner died?

I'm not really sure if it's been most days. I haven't kept track of it like that. The days just sort of... blend together now. I know it started after he passed, but I couldn't tell you if I've felt this way most days out of the week. I just know I sit in my chair a lot now.
Since your bowling partner died, have you found yourself longing for him or feeling a strong sense of missing him?

No, not really. I mean, it was sad when he passed, but we were just bowling partners. We weren't close friends outside of the alley or anything. I don't sit around missing him specifically... it's just that after it happened, everything else just sort of stopped mattering to me.
Before your bowling partner died, had you ever gone through another period in your life when you lost interest in things like this for a while?

No, I don't think so. I can't really remember ever feeling quite like this before. I've always been pretty active, you know, keeping busy with things. But this... this is different. I've never just stopped caring about everything like this.
Have you been having trouble concentrating, like following a TV show, reading, or keeping track of a conversation?

Yes, it's been very hard to focus. I used to help out with the senior center budgets, but I just can't keep the numbers straight anymore. I'll sit there and stare at a bill, or even just a calendar, for half an hour... and I just don't understand what I'm supposed to do with it. My mind just goes blank.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

No, not really. I seem to sleep alright. I mean, I haven't noticed any issues falling asleep or waking up in the middle of the night or anything like that. My sleep is pretty much just... the same as it usually is.
Have you noticed your appetite has gone down?
No, I haven't really noticed any change there. I... I still eat my regular meals. My appetite seems to be about the same as it always is.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Yes, my wife has mentioned it. She says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. And... well, she's right. Even just trying to get dressed in the morning, or walking across the kitchen... it takes me so long now. Most of the time I just end up giving up before I’ve really done much of anything.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yes, I have. I just... I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with him, and with my family. It just plays in my head. I feel like I’m no good to anybody anymore. And... honestly, I know I deserve whatever punishment is coming to me for all of it.
During this past year, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yes... yes, definitely. It's been like this for... for months now, really. Just this heavy, dark feeling all day, every day. I can't seem to shake it.
Before your bowling partner died, had you already been feeling depressed most days for at least two years?

No, no, it wasn't like this before he passed. I mean, sure, I'd have a bad day here or there like anyone else, but... not this. This constant heaviness, it really only started after he died. Before that, I was doing alright.
Has this made it hard for you to manage your usual daily activities?

Yes, it really has. I just... I can't keep up with things anymore. I used to be dependable, you know, at the senior center and around the house. But now I've just stopped doing any of it. My wife has had to take over everything—paying the bills, keeping track of the calendar, making all the decisions I used to handle. I just can't do it. And... well, my family and my pastor got so scared by the things I was saying that they basically pushed me to get urgent help. They saw I wasn't managing at all.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or high, much more than your normal self?
No... no, I haven't. I've never felt anything like that. Before all this started, I was just... just my normal self. I've never had a time where I felt unusually high or full of energy.
